title: The Magic Barrier: A Universal Feature of Quantum Thermalization
authors: Jakob J. Minar, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl
abstract: We show that the emergence of a ``magic barrier'', characterized by a transient maximum of nonstabilizerness during rapid entanglement growth, is a universal feature of thermalization within quantum ergodic theories, which is intimately connected to random matrix spectral properties. Starting from a pure product state, we analytically determine the time evolution of entanglement entropy, antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal trace distance magic under unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from all three Gaussian ensembles. We find that the transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth. These results establish that the magic barrier is a universal feature of RMT thermalization, suggesting universality across quantum chaotic systems. We conclude that quantitative simulations of thermalization in ergodic quantum theories inherently require quantum computation.
summary: This work proves that a 'magic barrier'—a transient peak in nonstabilizerness—is a universal feature characterizing quantum thermalization in systems governed by random matrix statistics. By analyzing entanglement entropy and related measures, the authors show this barrier appears simultaneously with the maximum rate of entanglement growth. The findings suggest that understanding thermalization in chaotic quantum systems requires advanced theoretical tools, potentially necessitating quantum computation for full quantitative description.
main_problem: To establish that the 'magic barrier'—a transient maximum of nonstabilizerness during rapid entanglement growth—is a universal feature of quantum thermalization in ergodic quantum theories.
main_result: The transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth, establishing the magic barrier as a universal feature of RMT thermalization.
method: Analytical determination of the time evolution of multiple quantum information measures using ensemble averaging techniques derived from random matrix theory.
model_or_system: Quantum systems undergoing unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from Gaussian ensembles (GOE, GUE, GSE). The analysis is performed in the large N limit.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy, Antiflatness, Capacity of entanglement, and Nonlocal Trace Distance Magic (NLTDM).
important_parameters: Large N limit, characteristic timescale of entanglement growth, and the specific Gaussian ensembles (GOE, GUE, GSE).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large N limit and the assumption that the system obeys Random Matrix Theory (RMT) level statistics.
figures_summary: Figures compare numerical dynamics of the four measures against analytical large N results, showing the transient peak (magic barrier) and confirming predicted scaling laws for finite-size corrections.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem and key observables to deriving time evolutions using four-point correlators, establishing the universal timescale coincidence, and finally confirming results via numerical simulations and bounding deviations.
why_interesting: It provides a universal, quantifiable signature (the magic barrier) for how quantum systems approach thermal equilibrium, linking quantum information measures directly to the underlying spectral statistics of chaotic dynamics.
